[spoiler=One big mistake][b]June 29, 2026[/b]
The SS Kalvinax (originally IPEA Ship #122) was a medium bulk carrier. It housed 134 (Baladullah and Wesernian) men and women on board, as well as 10,000 tons of coal (worth 1,030,000 ₩). It was crossing in between Baladullah and Kolionia when a smuggled submarine found it. The sub only had one torpedo thus only one shot. It hit the SS Kalvinax right in between water-tight compartment 6 and 7. She sank in less than 10 minutes, killing 104 people on board, including 51 Baladullahians. There are records of a submarine that was smuggled from Wessernian by Guhui'Bernardio, and soon after, sunk near the wreck of the Kalvinax. When they found the wreck of the sub, the one torpedo had been missing, and torpedo of the same size hit the Kavinax. It was soon apparent that Guhui'Bernardio had killed 51 Baladullahians, and sunk millions of westerns worth in coal.[/spoiler]
[spoiler= Hatzur Zatsugi's Final Favor
Chapter 2: The day of reckoning][b]July 13, 2026[/b]
13 was a lucky number in Wessernian practices, but 13 was also the date of the SS Leviathans sinking, and the murder of 38. 1 year was how long ago that happened, and it still stained Western View today. Some of the northern beaches' water was still black, stained by a continuing crisis. 13 was also the day when Hatzur Zatsugi returned, and now he was waging war. 

[b][i]7:13[/i][/b]

As the sun came up, a helicopter came down, a helicopter carrying the worlds most wanted. He stepped out onto the destroyer over looking Wessernia. As he walked up to the bridge many people were just getting out of bed, some woken up by the helicopter, others reminded that they were awake by the helicopter. Once he arrived at the bridge, a young man handed Hatzur a radio. "All troops, execute order 68" Hatzur said, and at that moment, the world became louder with motors, guns, and shouts.

[b][i]7:33[/i][/b]

It took another ten minutes for all the troops to land, but they had all the time in the world. Western View was unprepared for something like this, for any declaration of war would give them plenty of time to prepare. At least that is what civilians thought. If you worked in the military or the government, you would know that there are guns, just not visible. As the troops landed the guns arose from the sand on rails. Controlled by people in a government bunker, these guns were worth most of the military spending on the army. Even if Wessernian army money went to these guns, a seemingly unending amount off-shore bombardment would take a toll on them, even if they weren't accurate. The only thing the Guhui'Bernardio hadn't accounted for was friendly fire. Almost immediately the ship crews realized they were killing their own men and stopped. That's when Hatzur Zatsugi yelled on the radio "Why are we not bombarding them, continue now!"

"But the men on the shore will die," Retorted one gunner.

"So! More men will die if you do not bombard the shores!" Hatzur yelled back.

"Men! We must take up arms to stop this madness," Yelled the same gunner. After that many "Yeahs!" cheers and hoots were heard over the radio.

"Special Units, take over the ships, kill any who try to resist, and continue order 68" Hatzur said before exiting the bridge.[/spoiler]

Expansion Post: Ghijand
[spoiler] The Ghijandi peoples first arrived in their modern geographic area in around the 400s. Settlers from the northern mountains of Aekarxa migrated down south to the Shaki Valley in search of a more suitable climate for crops, after a brutal winter had ravaged the sub-Arctic areas of East Shamat. The settlers founded the Kingdom of Ghijand in around 630 CE. The kingdom chose the town of Naryn, at the time a small settlement based around grain farming.

Ghijand began to grow quickly, as its strategic position behind the Shaki mountains in the eastern steppes made it both difficult to invade and easy to trade and maintain order in the flat and hilly terrain. Grain farming turned successful in the new land, allowing the capital of Naryn to flourish and become a larger scale hub. A modest palace was constructed in 778, serving as the home for the monarchy.

Ghijand began to suffer internal strife and instability in the 1100s, due to political corruption and a severe drought that had brought the economy to its knees. It also didnt help that the new states of Hydronia and Srpka were rapidly growing in power, reducing Ghijands regional influence. Thanks to Ghijands relatively impressive military, the kingdom never devolved into civil war, however it failed to effectively keep up with the growing powers around it.

Ghijand suffered from General Badais wars, when Badai unified Alaqar for the first time and went on a campaign of conquest. In these conquests, Ghijand put up a staunch resistance to the invasion, even briefly pushing back Badais forces. Nevertheless, it still fell under his thumb until he died, in which Ghijand regained its independence in 1313 during the Second Fracturing.

Ghijand was given a chance to take back regional control, with the First Srpkan-Hydronian War. Mercenaries from Ghijand were sent to both sides of the conflict, and in exchange for fighting for either side, coin was coughed up to Ghijand. Ghijand saw the war as a way to weaken both sides of the conflict, hopefully to prevent either faction from dominating the other. The money gained from the exchange was enough to keep the state afloat.

From this point on, the new Ghijandi kingdom flourished. Economic and political reforms were put in place to guide the state away from the old kingdoms failures, helping stabilize the nation after decades of instability. The military was given modern weapons and technology thanks to their connections to the outside East Shamatine powers. Luxury goods and fine silks were made in Ghijand and exported to far away lands. The years between 1320 and 1677 are considered the Golden Era of Ghijand. 

The royal palace in Naryn was refurbished and the capital as a whole became a major trading center for East Shamat. The kingdom moved away from grain production and farming, instead placing a focus on trade and becoming an export based market. With the focus on trade, Ghijand gained info and resources for the ever changing environment of warfare, being forced to adapt their own military with muskets and other firearms for the time.

Ghijand was there to witness the Second Srpkan-Hydronian War, in which it had again played for both sides of the conflict. However, Ghijand leaned a little harder on Srpkas side due to the fear of the Holy Hydronic Empire and its growing influence. With the wars end ending in neither side securing a clear victory, Ghijand was safe again, and allowed to remain to its own devices once again, continuing to prosper under its quickly modernizing political and economic system.

The Third Srpkan-Hydronian War struck East Shamat, and Ghijand yet again acted in both sides. The war saw Ghijandi military capabilities reach their peak, with Ghijandi mercenaries becoming famed for their bravery in battle where others wouldve cowered. In reality, the mercenaries were just in it for the sake of money and honor, but the Srpkans had a tradition of telling tall tales about their exploits, of which Ghijandis were often found to be praised and revered in song.

In 1587, Ghijand established a parliamentary assembly to counterbalance the powers of the monarch, allowing for the streamlining of political affairs within the state. Although the state wasnt ready to fall apart, the kingdom did see a decline as the decades went on. In 1677, Ghijands golden age finally came to a close with the Srpkan incursion into Bozor. Bozor had been going through extreme internal violence, in which Srpka had taken advantage of, conquering and integrating the state within the Khanate. 

Ghijand began facing similar unrest from within, with the monarchy becoming increasingly weak and unstable, leading to mass protests and riots in the major cities. The Ghijandi government attempted to take back control of the state, but was unsuccessful when the rioters burst through the gates of the palace and launched a coup of the monarchy. In its place a republic was established, with surprisingly little resistance from internal powers due to the shared distrust in the monarchy.

The Srpkan Khanate launched an invasion 11 days later amidst fears of republican ideals spreading to Srpka and causing unrest. The new Ghijandi government organized the military quickly and sent them to the frontlines, where they maintained a strong defense against the Khanate. The Srpkan army had logistical troubles crossing the Shaki mountains, had just fought a war in Bozor, and lacked motivation to attack a nation which had done very little to deserve violence. The Ghijandis had a disciplined, concentrated army, a mountain range to defend with and a will to defend their homeland.

The 40,000 Srpkan soldiers sent to conquer Ghijand were quickly sent on the retreat within a week, and within a month, Ghijandi forces were crossing into Qar-Shaki. The government of Qar-Shaki sent a letter to the Khan, saying to sign peace with the Ghijandis as they were now crossing into Srpkan land. The Khan caved and signed a peace treaty with the new government the same year he invaded, seeing no reason to pursue an expensive campaign for a nation a mountain range away.

The Ghijandi government did not intervene in the Srpkan invasion of Hydronia even as it attracted smaller powers like Sakara. The mercenaries that had joined the last few wars were now few and far between, as the Holy Hydronic Empire was now weakening and Srpka strengthening, there was little reason to join up on either side to prevent the conquest of their homeland.

The following decades after 1730 were peaceful for Ghijand. The state found peace and stability within its new republic, turning the palace into a place for the executive office to live. The republic improved the infrastructure in the state, connecting towns and cities by road and providing transportation for rural areas. The republic also provided the foundation for a new national currency, replacing the old currency with a much stabler and stronger dollar. 

Ghijand did well politically and economically, diversifying its economy to pursue a more self-sufficient economic policy. The state began to develop ties with the Srpkans, seeing them as a potential future ally. The capital of Ghijand, Naryn, was becoming a major industrial center thanks to its flat terrain allowing for heavy construction over factories and railroads, something that was greatly appreciated as the world began industrializing.

Ghijand watched as Srpka found itself in an 8 year long religious revolution with Islamic revolutionaries who felt they were being oppressed by the rest of the population and the government. Ghijand had a very small population of Muslims, and treated their minorities relatively well compared to Srpka, so they did not receive a revolutionary movement like the Srpkans did.

The revolution eventually ended, and ties between the Srpkans and Ghijandis became even stronger. Ghijand had historically had a strong sense of independence, contributing to the survival of the state, however it also lacked the benefits of a larger power to support it if it ever broke. The Srpkans had finally created a stable government promising ethnic equality and religious liberty, embedding it into their own constitution. The Ghijandis finally felt that they could safely join the Srpkans, without the fear of racism or ethnic discrimination. On January 11th, 1829, the Republic of Ghijand officially joined the Khanate of Srpka, ending 700 years of independence and stepping into a new era, now with someone to hold their hand.
[/spoiler]

[b]The Five Angels[/b]

With the reopening of Ascoiya to the world stage, Socialist International would express an interest in influencing the nascent power to the cause of the people's revolution. Though, with Qianxun currently completely invested in the Astaniran Civil War to realistic pursue investments, the trouble of reopening Ascoiya to global markets would fall upon the "Five Angels"Almstedt Corporation, Tarta Energy Corporation "Tencor", Qianxun United Armor Corporation "Qunarco", Miwu Group, and Somare S.p.A., an [i]ad hoc[/i] international cartel of corporations known for their controversial ties with Socialist International and the Min Zhu Party.

Almstedt Corporation, a Vespurian conglomerate based in the State of Norrhollow, would be the most powerful of the Five and the most notorious due to the actions of its subsidiaries, particular SummitONE Solutions, which is currently blacklisted in several nations thanks to its involvement in the Balizian insurgency, the Sikirskian Civil War, and allegedly the Astaniran Civil War. Still though, with the Ascoiyan government literally cut off from most international events until recently, the time was ripe for the Almstedts and the other Angel corporations to step up and help a struggling new global player. With the backing of the Qianxun and Sanguinian state governments, the Five Angels would send representatives to Ascoiya seeking to begin operations within the country.

In addition to the typical arrangements sought by foreign investors like tax-friendly business zones and relaxed trade barriers, the Five Angels would take the unconventional step of asking the Ascoiyan government to also establish a modern ship register, which may be undertaken online (with digital infrastructure that may also be funded by the corporations), with exemption on income taxes, and the ability to hire Ascoiyan laborers subject to deregulated minimum wages. In return, the Five Angels would offer generous discounts on oil exports for the first year of operation, mostly to aid the nation to transition to a more oil-dependent economy that will necessitate further imports.

SummitONE would also note Ascoiya's dated port infrastructure and recommend its [url=https://www.nationstates.net/page=rmb/postid=58820923]Seagates program[/url] to facilitate Ascoiya's swift introduction to international shipping lanes, should they be interested.
